Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior

Enum Class EyeBehavior

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<EyeBehavior>
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeBehavior
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<EyeBehavior>, Constable
public enum EyeBehavior extends Enum<EyeBehavior>
The seven named eye expressions a mob can play, keyed by a ResourceLocation id. These are code-defined client animations, and both sides only need the ids to agree: the server names a behavior by id in the trigger packet and the client looks it up to play. All per-play state lives in a BehaviorInstance.

A mob plays at most one behavior at a time (the server enforces this), so behaviors never compose. They participate in the eye physics simulation, not the renderer: once per simulation tick the simulator asks the single active behavior to fill an EyeInfluence per eye — a pupil spring (anchor + stiffness) and/or the non-physical overlays (scale, squash, tint). The renderer then just interpolates and draws the resulting eye state; it never touches behaviors.

This type must stay free of client-only imports: the server class-loads it to pick and schedule behaviors, and only the client ever calls influence(com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.BehaviorInstance, int, int, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeInfluence).

  • Enum Constant Details

    • STARE

      public static final EyeBehavior STARE
      Pupils are sprung to center and held, then released so they drop back into the physics wobble. A center spring whose stiffness eases in, holds, and eases back out; when it fades, gravity carries the pupil down naturally (no snap).

    • BLINK

      public static final EyeBehavior BLINK
      Squashes between 1 and N of the mob's eyes shut and open again. The participating set is chosen once from the seed, so a "wink" (one eye) and a full blink are the same behavior at different counts. Non-physical overlay: drives the squash channel only — the pupil keeps wobbling underneath.

    • GROW

      public static final EyeBehavior GROW
      Eyes briefly bulge larger and settle back. Non-physical overlay: drives the eye-scale channel.

    • COLOR_CHANGE

      public static final EyeBehavior COLOR_CHANGE
      Blends the cornea toward a color and back. The color is chosen from the seed (a random hue). Non-physical overlay: drives the cornea-tint channel.

    • SWIRL

      public static final EyeBehavior SWIRL
      Pupils orbit rapidly, the orbit radius shrinking to zero so they spiral into the center as the effect ends. A firm spring to a moving anchor; because the anchor itself spirals to center, the pupil ends near center and the release is soft (no drop from the rim).

    • SIDE_EYE

      public static final EyeBehavior SIDE_EYE
      Pupils are sprung to center, then the anchor slides slowly to one side (chosen from the seed) and holds there before the spring releases. The stiffness eases in during the brief centering and out at the very end, so the held side-glance drops back to physics naturally.

    • CROSS_EYE

      public static final EyeBehavior CROSS_EYE
      Pupils are sprung to center, then their anchors slide toward each eye's configured cross-target — the other eye it should look at (EyePlacement.crossTarget(), an index within the same head) — and hold before the spring releases. Each eye aims the direction to its partner, projected into its own pupil plane, so convergence is correct regardless of how many eyes a head has or how they're aimed. An eye with no configured target (the default) simply doesn't cross.
